title: FeatureImportance maxVal uses items[0].importance, wrong for negative/zero importances
description: maxVal is taken as `items[0]?.importance || 1` on the assumption that the first (descending-sorted) feature is the largest by magnitude. Bar width is then `(Math.abs(fi.importance) / Math.abs(maxVal)) * 100%` (line 60), which uses absolute values. The backend sorts feature_importance / feature_importance_loss by RAW value descending, not by absolute value (src/haute/modelling/_algorithms.py:620-624 and 639-643 `sorted(..., key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)`), and CatBoost LossFunctionChange importances can be negative (no abs/clip applied; _result_types.py:19). Consequences on the 'Loss' tab: (a) a feature with a large NEGATIVE importance sorts LAST, so its |importance| can exceed |items[0].importance|, yielding a bar width > 100% (overflow); (b) if items[0].importance is itself negative, Math.abs(maxVal) is a small positive denominator and ALL bars are massively over-scaled; (c) if items[0].importance === 0, `0 || 1` forces maxVal=1, mis-scaling every bar. The hardened sibling FeaturesTab.tsx computes `maxVal = items.map(i => Math.abs(i.importance)).reduce((a,b)=>Math.max(a,b), -Infinity)` (FeaturesTab.tsx:46) and guards the denominator with `maxVal > 0 ? ... : '0%'` (FeaturesTab.tsx:91). Existing FeatureImportance tests only use positive descending importances, so this is uncovered.
evidence: FeatureImportance.tsx:28 `const maxVal = items[0]?.importance || 1` -> :60 `width: ${(Math.abs(fi.importance)/Math.abs(maxVal))*100}%`. Backend _algorithms.py:620-624 sorts by raw value desc; LossFunctionChange may be negative; _result_types.py:19 stores it unmodified. Correct pattern in FeaturesTab.tsx:46,91.
